newsitem.title: USA: USAir pilots inch towards tentative pact.
newsitem.headline: USAir pilots inch towards tentative pact.

text.p: USAir Group Inc and its pilots union have inched closer to a tentative labor pact but remain far apart on several meaty issues, sources familiar with the situation said.
Union and company officials declined to comment.
While the agreement is on a relatively minor issue, the accord is the first positive step towards reaching a broader labor settlement, sources said.
The tentative pact centers on training and pay levels for senior level pilots, sources said.
Normally, senior pilots approaching retirement apply or "bid" for higher-paying jobs in their last few years to bolster their pensions. The training for those jobs can be costly.

The airline and the union have now tentatively agreed to allow those pilots to be bumped to the higher pay level. But instead of training pilots who will soon leave the company upon retirement, the airline would train younger pilots who for those positions.
The deal would protect the senior pilots' pay but allow the company to get more years of service from younger pilots, sources said.
The pilots and the company still wrestle with several major issues, such as the formation of a low-cost unit and pay levels.
The company seeks paycuts of about 12.5 percent from its pilots, sources said. The proposed paycuts differ strongly from double-digit pay increases being sought at other airlines.
